title: Hubline: Simplify Console Navigation and Workspace Flow
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Customers and internal users encounter cognitive overhead when moving between workspace contexts, dashboard metrics (cost/latency), and rollout controls. Current left-rail is dense, mixes global vs project-scoped routes, and has inconsistent workspace-switch affordances. Goal: Deliver a simplified, tiered navigation pattern (Hubline) that reduces clicks to core tasks, surfaces cost & rollout primary metrics in a contextual panel, and provides a predictable workspace-switch flow. Scope: IA changes to left rail + top context bar, a collapsible contextual panel for 'Cost & Rollouts', updated route hierarchy for projects/environments, and a high-fidelity prototype for user testing. Out of scope: backend routing enforcement, RBAC policy changes (handled by Eng), major telemetry collection (follow-up). Constraints: Must work at 1024–1440px widths, respect current brand tokens, and degrade gracefully in narrow screens. Must integrate with existing Console routes (no breaking route URLs).
acceptance_criteria: Left-rail reorganized into three tiers: global actions, workspaces/projects, and quick-actions. Visual design and IA approved by PM and Eng.
Workspace switch flow reduced to a single primary click + keyboard shortcut; tests show median workflow time improvement >20% in prototype study.
Contextual 'Cost & Rollouts' panel surfaces top-level metrics (7d spend delta, per-request latency p95, active canaries) and links to detailed dashboards.
Prototype v0.3 linked and tested with 6 internal users; issues tracked and prioritized.
Design handoff artifacts (tokens, spacing, component spec) uploaded to the design library and linked to PRs for implementation.
No route collisions with existing URLs; routing fallback documented for Eng.
Accessibility checks: left-rail items have 44px touch targets, keyboard focus order validated, and color contrast passes AA for primary text.
Final design sign-off from Design Lead and PM (signatures in comments).
